production.note: US model years of the coupe. First: MBUSA's '2017 C-Class Coupe Quick Reference Guide' lists the AMG C63 S Coupe. Last: Cars.com lists an 'AMG C 63 S Coupe' trim for 2021 (carscom-2021-c63) and for 2022 shows only the 'AMG C 63 S Cabriolet' (carscom-2022-c63). The C 63 S Sedan (W205) is a separate record.

fuel.note: Inferred from the description of the V8 biturbo petrol engine.

transmission.note: 2017-2018: 'AMG SPEEDSHIFT MCT 7-speed transmission' (2018 sheet; the 2017 guide: 'AMG SPEEDSHIFT MCT 7-speed sport Transmission'). 2019-2021: the facelifted C63 got the 'AMG SPEEDSHIFT MCT 9G' (carscoops-2019-c63, Michael Gauthier: 'the engine is now connected to an AMG SPEEDSHIFT MCT 9G transmission', naming the 2019 C63 Coupe and Cabriolet; gtspirit-2019-c63, Earl Karanja: 'Saloon, Estate, Coupé and Cabriolet' ... 'AMG Speedshift MCT 9G transmission'). MCT is a planetary automatic with a wet start-up clutch in place of the torque converter.

powerHp.note: Quote: "Horsepower | 469 @ 5,500-6,250 (C 63) | 503 @ 5,500-6,250 (C 63 S)". The 2017 guide (mbusa-2017-c-class-coupe-qrg): "C63 S: 503 hp @ 5,500". The non-S C 63 (469 hp) is a separate variant.

weightLb.note: US manufacturer curb weight, C63 S Coupe with the only transmission (7-speed MCT), 2017 model year (weight-order step 1). Quote (2017 guide): "Curb weight ... C63: 4,074 / C63 S: 4,096". The 2018 sheet gives the same: "4,096" (mbusa-2018-c63-coupe-specs). No MBUSA coupe sheet for 2019-2021 was found.

sources.title: 2018 Mercedes-AMG C 63 Coupe and C 63 S Coupe Specifications

reviewNotes: The last coupe model year (2021) rests on Cars.com trim listings; no MBUSA page for a 2019-2021 C 63 S Coupe was opened, and the 9-speed for those years rests on two named-author outlets. Body decision (3 October 2026, owner): the Sedan and the Coupe are separate cars in the game.
